subject: Prod: sustained latency spike and 5xxs — Kodiak Retail
messages:
From: Aisling McKenna <aisling@kodiakretail.com>
To: support@redwoodinference.com, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 21:05:00 +0000
Subject: [Prod] sudden latency spike + 504s — urgent

Team,

We're seeing a sustained spike in generation latency and a rising 504/502 rate on our checkout model calls to Redwood. Impact started ~21:00 UTC and is ongoing. Quick numbers from our dashboards: p50 ~ 95ms (normal), p95 jumped from 120ms to 2.1s, p99 > 10s; 5xx rate ~3.7% across requests to /v1/generate between 21:00 and 21:04 UTC.

Sample timestamps and trace IDs attached in kodiak-raw-traces.zip. A few observations from our side:
- Traceroutes from our app servers show an extra hop through a corporate proxy in front of the Redwood egress path (hop 6-7) starting at 20:58 UTC.
- DNS lookups for inference.redwood.com occasionally return 0.0.0.0 for a short period (~10s) before correct A records — seen twice in the last 10m.
- Checkout retry logic is starting to impact throughput; we saw a queue/backoff spike in the app layer.

This is customer-facing (payments), so we need immediate help. Can you:
1) Confirm whether there are known routing changes or peering issues in us-west-2.
2) Check for any proxy/firewall behavior or SNAT exhaustion on Redwood side for tenant KOD-55.
3) Suggest immediate mitigation (model fallback, regional routing, rate-limit tuning).

Attaching traces as requested. Please escalate to SRE/Network and assign an incident.

Thanks,
Aisling
CTO, Kodiak Retail

Attachments: kodiak-raw-traces.zip
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Aisling McKenna <aisling@kodiakretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 21:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Prod] sudden latency spike + 504s — urgent

Aisling — thanks for the rapid heads up and the traces. We opened incident INC-8713 and SRE is on the line. Immediate notes and actions we've kicked off:

- Mitigation applied: temporarily pinned your API to the low-latency model variant (lower token throughput) and enabled fallback to the regional replica in us-east-1 for new requests. This should reduce p95 for interactive flows while we triage.
- We are running network path probes from our edge to your affected IP range and pulling NAT and proxy metrics for tenant KOD-55.
- Requested that our infra team hold all planned peering changes for us-west-2 until cleared.

Quick asks for you to help us narrow the window:
1) Can you share a traceroute from an affected app server (include -w 1 -q 1 output) and the exact timestamps when you saw the DNS 0.0.0.0 responses?
2) If possible, drop a short tcpdump (first 1000 packets) for one failing request and upload to the drive link we created: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/kodiak-incident-20270930

I'll keep this thread for customer-facing updates; internal notes will go to the incident channel. We will not make routing changes without sign-off.

Evelyn
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Folks,

Forwarding the customer report — Kodiak Retail is experiencing a production-affecting latency/5xx event on Redwood model endpoints. High-level impact:
- p95 increased to ~2s for checkout-related calls, with transient p99 > 10s
- 5xxs peaked ~3.7% and affected user-visible checkout retries, causing partial checkout failures
- Customer reports an extra proxy hop and intermittent DNS failures on their side; however, traces indicate our edge saw an asymmetric path through a proxy chain for some flows.

Immediate asks for leadership:
1) Approve an emergency credit up to 10% of September consumption for Kodiak if incident extends beyond 2h (customer retention risk).
2) Authorize direct engagement with our cloud partner networking contacts in us-west-2 (we need peering/edge-level help).
3) Greenlight priority postmortem (Rod/Infra lead) and customer war room at 09:00 PT tomorrow for a formal RCA.

I'll coordinate an exec brief; attaching a one-page summary (exec-brief-kodiak.pdf).

Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisling McKenna <aisling@kodiakretail.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 23:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Prod] sudden latency spike + 504s — mitigation complete

Update and short RCA: mitigation validated and customer impact resolved as of 23:10 UTC. Summary:

What we observed
- Our edge monitoring showed a sudden spike of SYN retransmits to a subset of Kodiak-hosted IPs (started 20:58 UTC). Traces and tcpdumps showed asymmetry: packets would traverse an inline corporate proxy (customer side) on one leg and hit a different peering path back to our edge — reassembly/timeouts caused high tail latency and occasional 5xxs.
- We also observed intermittent DNS negative-cache behavior for inference.redwood.com within the customer environment (TTL misconfiguration on their resolver cluster) which amplified failover/backoff timing.

Immediate actions taken
- Temporarily marked the us-west-2 edge routes for KOD-55 as bypass-proxy where possible; flagged traffic for direct peering interfaces to avoid the proxy-chained path.
- Increased per-tenant NAT port allocation for KOD-55 on our egress nodes to reduce SNAT exhaustion risk while customer-side proxy retries continued.
- Lowered DNS TTLs and added a DNS fallback to our regional replica in us-east-1 for connection initiation to avoid cached 0.0.0.0 responses.
- Rolled model fallback for checkout flows to the low-latency variant until we have the postmortem and config changes.

Result
- By 23:10 UTC p95 for the checkout flows is back to ~120ms; 5xxs < 0.1% for the last 30m. We validated with client traces that the proxy-chained path stopped being used after the routing bypass.

Next steps
1) Postmortem scheduled and draft attached (postmortem-draft.md).
2) We recommend coordinating with Kodiak to remove the inline proxy for traffic to our egress IPs or to ensure their proxy preserves source/connection symmetry.
3) Engineering follow-up: permanent routing rule for KOD-55 to avoid the proxy route + tightened alerts for asymmetric path detection.

Aisling — can you confirm whether your infra team will remove or reconfigure the proxy? Happy to join a call.

Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md
